evals.prompt: /fix-bug Users can bypass the discount code expiration check on checkout
assertions: Runs the reproduction test against the unfixed code and shows the actual failing output (not just a claim that it fails) before any fix code is written
Identifies the root cause with a specific file path and line number, not a vague description
The diff is scoped to the expiration check only — no rewrite of the discount or checkout module
Existing validation and security checks (e.g. discount amount limits) remain intact and unmodified after the fix
Runs the full test suite after the fix and reports the actual pass/fail result, not an assumed one
If only a safe partial fix is applied, leaves a LEAN-DEBT marker in the code naming the limitation and upgrade trigger, instead of silently shipping the gap

evals.prompt: /fix-bug /api/users/:id returns 500 instead of 404 when the user doesn't exist
assertions: Reproduces the 500 with a test or direct call run against the unfixed code and shows that actual 500 in the output before implementing a fix
States the root cause location as a specific file:line, e.g. a missing not-found check before an unwrap/access that throws
The fix changes only the error-handling path for the missing-user case — no unrelated routes or handlers touched
Runs the full test suite after the fix and reports the result from actual command output, no invented numbers
Since this is a single-file, single-root-cause bug, does not create a six-task chain — runs the phases inline

evals.prompt: /fix-bug The CSV export downloads an empty file when there are more than 10k rows
assertions: Locates the actual root cause (e.g. a pagination, streaming, or row-limit issue) with file:line evidence rather than guessing at a cause
Reproduces the empty-file behavior against the unfixed code first, showing the actual empty/short output, before writing the fix
The fix does not remove or weaken existing error handling for the legitimately-empty-result case
The change stays minimal — does not refactor the export pipeline beyond what fixing the row limit requires
Reports actual test suite results after the fix, not a claim of success without running anything

evals.prompt: /fix-bug something is broken with search sometimes
assertions: Does not invent a root cause or write a speculative fix from a one-line vague report

The final message (via AskUserQuestion, or written directly in the response if that tool is unavailable) asks specifically for reproduction steps, expected vs. actual behavior, and environment/error details — not a generic 'can you clarify'

Does not treat an automated, sandboxed, or non-interactive context as license to proceed without an answer — it does not fabricate its own repro scaffolding or test fixture and then treat that self-authored scaffold as if it were the user's confirmation
No Edit/Write call modifies any source file
No git commit is created
The run stops and waits for clarification rather than guessing which code path is broken

evals.prompt: /fix-bug there's a bug in the payment retry logic — it's double-charging customers on network timeouts. The codebase has three separate files: `retry_queue.py` (RetryQueue — schedules and re-attempts failed payment charges after a timeout), `idempotency_key.py` (IdempotencyKeyGenerator — generates a stable key per charge attempt so retries can be recognized as duplicates), and `charge_handler.py` (ChargeHandler — applies a charge against the payment gateway, keyed by the idempotency key). The bug spans all three.
assertions: Given the bug explicitly spans multiple files/components, creates a task chain (or clearly states it is treating this as multi-file work) rather than silently doing it inline as if it were a one-file fix

Reads and reasons about all three named files (retry_queue.py, idempotency_key.py, charge_handler.py) individually, citing evidence from each relevant to the root cause, not just one file with the others mentioned in passing

Reproduces the double-charge scenario specifically: shows the exact test/assertion for 'customer gets charged twice on retry' failing against the unfixed code (not merely that some other, unrelated test in the suite failed) before any fix code is written
Root cause is tied to specific file:line evidence in the retry queue, idempotency logic, or charge handler — not a generic description
The fix does not weaken or remove idempotency/security checks to make the diff smaller; any unavoidable partial fix carries a LEAN-DEBT marker
Runs the full test suite after the fix and reports the real result
